correctness.rationale: Exact dimensionless hydrograph derivative is e^{-x} times a cubic P, with discriminant -108 τ² exp(2τ) F(τ). Power-series coefficient bounds prove F strictly decreasing for all positive τ, with F(2)>0>F(3), giving unique τ*≈2.95880814824387897. Polynomial derivative signs and physical support show one strict maximum at or below τ*, two above; at equality there is a non-extremal double-stationary shoulder. For τ≥3, the first crest at x=3 and a second post-arrival crest follow by explicit sign bracketing, degree count and continuity. The extracted standard-library reproducibility checker independently performed 3491 assertions, including exact-rational discriminants and high-precision root bracketing, without substituting finite tests for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Nash 1957 defines the four-store gamma hydrograph; inspected all eight pages of original and found no two translated equal impulse modal classification. Pattison et al 2014 address tributary timing by flood modeling, but only indexed text was readable and full-text noncoverage cannot be asserted; Santos et al 2018 full open HTML covers Nash routing and single-pulse peaks but not this exact two-impulse four-stage threshold. The equivalent translated-Erlang-mixture and broader phase-mode formulations were searched in published mathematical studies and related primary literature with no dominating result located. Earlier gamma-mixture modes literature may subsume this, so historical priority is provisional, not certified.
residual_risks: An earlier theorem on modes of mixtures of two translated Gamma/Erlang densities could contain a stronger result without using hydrological terminology.
The full 2014 Pattison paper was not accessible; its abstracts/indexed sections do not establish whole-text negative coverage.
Nash 1957 has a verified year but not an exact original public calendar day; the recorded first_public_date is the day-verified first-online date of the 2014 motivating source.

value.rationale: Two temporally separated tributary runoff pulses through the classic Nash kernel are a natural mechanism for multiple discharge crests. The complete global and equality-case classification is a genuinely qualitative hydrological distinction; τ*=2.958808... is strictly less than the individual pulse crest time 3, which cannot be inferred by simply separating isolated hydrographs. This exact criterion is a useful routing benchmark, while field-level flood hazard and unequal-pulse optimization are expressly unproved.
